sources.entry: trekhleb/javascript-algorithms: algorithms and data structures implemented in JavaScript

summary.one_liner: A JavaScript collection of example implementations of many common algorithms and data structures, each with its own explanatory README.
summary.what_it_does: The repository holds JavaScript implementations of classic data structures (linked lists, stacks, queues, heaps, tries, trees including AVL and red-black, graphs, disjoint set, bloom filter, LRU cache) and algorithms grouped by topic (math, sets, strings, searches, sorting, graphs, cryptography, machine learning, image processing) and by paradigm (brute force, greedy, divide and conquer, dynamic programming, backtracking, branch and bound). The README says each item has its own separate README with explanations and further reading links, including YouTube videos. It also includes reference tables of Big O growth rates, data structure operation complexity, and array sorting complexity. Tests run with npm and a playground file is provided for experimenting.
use_cases: learning algorithms and data structures in JavaScript
looking up a JavaScript implementation of a specific algorithm
comparing time and space complexity of sorting and data structures
experimenting with code in a playground and running tests
notable: Covers a broad range of topics from linked lists to Knight's Tour, Seam Carving, and NanoNeuron
Each topic is tagged Beginner or Advanced
Algorithms are also organized by paradigm (greedy, backtracking, dynamic programming, etc.)
Includes Big O and sorting complexity reference tables
README is available in many languages
caveats: The README is a reference index; the detailed explanations live in per-topic READMEs not included in this text
Requires Node.js 16 or later to run lint and tests
